_readme: Controls which Halo MCP tools the voice agent can use. Rules are checked in order; first match wins.
kind: read | create_ticket | add_note | close_ticket | deny. 'match' is a tool name or a glob (* wildcard), case-insensitive.
ticketIdArg names the ticket ID parameter (add_note, close_ticket). omitArgs are hidden from Claude and stripped before the call.
Tools that match no rule are allowed only if the MCP server marks them readOnlyHint=true (and allowReadOnlyAnnotated is true).
Matched to the dhinternalitsm Halo Virtual Agent MCP catalogue (12 CF_ tools) on 2026-11-08. Re-check with `npm run list-tools` if the endpoint changes.
Write policy agreed for the PoC: create tickets, add notes to the caller's own tickets, and close a ticket created on this call when the issue was resolved on the call. Nothing else.

rules._why: Notes only: the status field could change any ticket's status, so it is hidden and stripped
Only tickets created on this call (resolved on the call); enforced in session.ts
A catalogue search; not annotated read-only, but it changes nothing
Lists every user's name and phone; used only by the pre-call lookup below

identify._readme: Pre-call caller lookup. {phone} in args is replaced with each phone format; with no {phone}, the tool is treated as a full user list and called once. Hits are kept only if the user's stored number equals the caller's. Delete this block to let the agent identify the caller itself.

promptNotes: The automatic caller lookup only gives a name. Always ask for the caller's work email address before logging a ticket, and use it as user_email.

Ticket search here is unreliable and often finds nothing. Ask the caller for the ticket number if they have one and use CF_get_one_ticket. Otherwise try CF_search_tickets with a few words describing the issue and open_only set to true. Only discuss or add notes to a ticket whose user_name matches the caller.

Assets in this Halo instance are not linked to users. To find the caller's device, ask for the asset tag on the sticker (for example ABC00001) or the model, then use CF_search_assets with that as the search term. Pass its id as asset_id when logging a ticket.
Search the knowledge base with CF_search_knowledge_base using a few key words from the symptoms. The results include the resolution steps; use CF_get_one_article only if you need more.

CF_log_incident needs user_email, a summary of 70 characters or less, a description, CFimpact (usually Single User Affected), CFurgency (usually Medium; High if the caller cannot work) and the closest category_1 from the list.
If the issue was fixed on the call, log the ticket with CF_log_incident, describing what fixed it, then close that ticket with CF_close_ticket. You can only close a ticket you created on this call.
CF_add_note adds a private note to a ticket. It cannot change the ticket's status.
